content.thinking:
I need to write this whole module in one pass without being able to test it, so I have to be extra careful about API correctness and unused imports. I'm sI'm planning out the qilin's proportions and skeleton structure in one pass, since I need to get the API right without testing—sizing it horse/deer-like with antlers, then working out the joint hierarchy with hips as root, spine chains to the neck and head, a tail chain, and leg chains for IK.

For the body geometry itself, I'm defining a spine path from rump to withers and figuring out how to sweep a tube along it, extending the start behind the pelvis joint with round caps so the body mesh connects cleanly to the hip root.

I'm deciding to split the neck into its own chain rather than including it in the spine, letting the neck tube start inside the chest with a larger radius so the round cap hides the seam, and planning to add a mane to cover the junction further. Now I'm setting up coordinates with +Z as forward and +X as the left side, working through the mirrored left/right joint loop.

For the legs, I'm giving the qilin hooves with slender deer-like limbs and digitigrade hind legs running hip to stifle to hock to fetlock to hoof, simplifying the front legs to three segments from shoulder to knee onward.

The joint direction indicates which wayI'm working out the two inner joint bends for the front leg (elbow backward, knee forward) and adjusting segment lengths to exceed the reach distance. Then I'm naming the four chain points—shoulder, elbow, knee, hoof—matching the three spans plus tip, and planning the polyline path structure for the limb.

For the hind legs, I'm setting hip and target positions and testing segment length combinations (thigh, gaskin, cannon) to see which sum best approximates the reach while keeping the cannon roughly vertical under the hock.

I'll place the foot slightly behind the hip, with the cannon angled parallel to the root-to-target direction, and set the hock bend hint accordingly so the last segment follows the hint-and-reach rule, defaulting to equal joint rotation otherwise.

For the hoof, I'll skip the pastern and make the tip a small frustum shape, adding fetlock tufts as flame-fur cards, with limbs straightening out when targets are out of reach. The neck will arc up from the spine end to the head using a catmull curve through several control points, parented to the last spine joint to get that horse-dragon arch look Qilin needs.

For the head, I'm thinking dragon-horse hybrid: a skull sphere with a tapering snout box for the muzzle, separate upper and lower jaws, nostrils, teeth, flowing whisker tendrils as swept rods, branching antlers, flame-fur cheek cards, and a beard, all stylized with oversized anime eyes for that elegant anime look -- jointed at the top of the neck.

Setting up the neck chain with three joints (neck1-3, no tip joint since spans match count), parented to the spine, with the head joint attached at the final neck joint, angled slightly forward and down.

For positioning the head, I'm clarifying that `.local()` offsets use world-aligned directions (forward/up/right etc.) rather than head-rotated axes, so I'll compute the head's actual coordinates using plain offsets from a head origin point rather than relying on local frame confusion.

Since parts placed with bare tuples default to the nearest joint, I should explicitly specify `bone: head` on all head parts. I'm setting up a head coordinate system relative to the head joint position, defining forward and up vectors tilted about 17° downward, and writing a helper function to compute points in this frame so I can place the skull and other head features precisely.

Still shaping the snout geometry...

Now I'm positioning the jaw bones: the upper head bone and a lower jaw bone with a hinge joint near the back of the mouth, aiming forward toward the snout tip. I'm deciding whether to keep the mouth closed with a slight gap or pose it a bit open to show the tongue.

I'll build the jaw geometry first then pose it open about 7 degrees at the end, since posing after the build means everything attached to the jaw -- teeth included -- moves naturally with the rotation. For teeth, I'm adding small spike-shaped fangs in the upper jaw and a smaller tusk in the lower jaw, plus a thin pink rod for the tongue.

Now I'm placing the nostrils as small dark spheres near the snout tip, with a cream-gold nose pad, and working out eye placement using the skin decal system -- positioning anime-style eyes on the skull by azimuth and elevation angles relative to the head's center, accounting for the skull's width and tilt so the eyes sit correctly on each side.

For the color palette, I'm leaning into a classic qilin look reimagined in anime high-fantasy style: a pearly white-cream body with jade/teal scales along the back and flanks, gold ornamental accents, a flowing mane gradient from turquoise to lilac, and gold antlers.

Defining paint and shading functions...

For the belly I'm using a zigzag teeth pattern along the z-axis, and for the mane I'm planning cloud-like swirls using textured cards with a teal-to-white-to-lilac gradient wisp shape across the neck, shoulders, cheeks, legs, and tail.

Writing SVG texture code...

That's the crest, so mane cards should flow back and down from the neck, leaning around 60 degrees, using a few angled rows for symmetry and tapered sizes. For the solid mane core I'm planning broad overlapping blade shapes plus some swept curved ribbons tapering in radius for a layered silhouette.

For curl details, I'm using spiral paths to create curled tips at the mane ends, tail, and chest — tapering tube radius down toward each curl's end with the axis set for side-facing swirls.

For the mane itself, I'm planning cloud-puff clusters of merged icospheres in white-lilac tones with cel shading, placed at shoulders and chest, keeping the part budget under roughly 600 by sharing geometry per bone and color.

For the antlers, which will be the creature's signature feature, I'm designing golden deer-like branching forms with jade tips that sweep back and up, built from bezier-based beams extending from the skull with three tines each.

Still plotting antler coordinates...

Tines angle forward-up-outward like classic deer antlers. For the tips, I'll add glowing jade octahedron crystals in cyan, plus gold torus rings around the beams aimed along the tangent direction at each point.

For color, I'm blending a gradient from warm gold at the base to pale jade near the tips using a sweep gradient applied with cel paint. Then for the ears, I'm shaping them like pointed elf-leaf fins, extruding a leaf-like outline along the side of the head.

I'm working out which plane the ear outline should sit in — since ears face sideways-forward, I need the leaf shape's normal oriented so it reads correctly from a front view rather than edge-on.

Now I'm thinking about facial detail: brow flames as tapered sweeps curving up and back over the eyes, probably colored gold-orange to match the dragon theme.

I'm also planning long flowing whiskers from the muzzle sides using curved sweeps that trail outward and down, tapering with a gold color, plus a beard tuft under the jaw rigidly attached to the head.

For cheek fur, I'm setting up ruff cards positioned with manual frames around the cheek region, oriented outward and leaning back, explicitly bound to the head bone. Now I'm moving on to the chest and other body details.

For body coloring, I'm adding flank scale paint with cream belly, then designing golden armor-style ornaments: a gold filigree collar with jade gem at the neck, gold cuffs with tassels above the legs, aiming for a qilin-inspired decorative look using surface loops swept around the neck joint.

Placing the pendant gem at the bottom of the neck loop, hanging down from the collar...

For body gold accents, I'm considering a girth strap around the belly using a cross-sectional loop perpendicular to the spine bone at a mid joint, since the spine runs horizontal-forward.

I'm placing gold studs evenly along that loop using a callback-based distribution function, then shifting to defining the spine chain itself, starting with the pelvis root joint position and orientation for the hip/spine hierarchy.

Building out the spine joints from hips through chest with a smooth curved path, then setting up the body sweep with radius functions controlling width and height along that spine to shape the torso silhouette.

Too tall compared to legs, so I'm scaling down to a slender deer-like proportion with body ry 0.22 and hips/chest centered around y 1.12-1.24, giving withers around 1.46 which matches a horse-like scale while keeping legs proportional with hip joints near y 1.05.

Now I'm working out the front and hind leg geometry, computing root-to-target reach distances and segment lengths to get natural bends at the knee and hock. The hind leg forms a triangle with the stifle bulging forward moderately, giving it a convincing horse-like hind leg shape, though I still need to check that the cannon bone segment runs parallel as expected.

For the hooves, I'm sizing a tapered cylinder frustum positioned so its base sits on the floor and its top meets the leg tube, then considering whether to make them cloven like a qilin's deer/ox-style hoof by splitting each into two offset half-hooves with a dark cleft line between them.

Now I'm adding decorative details like dewclaws and cloud-fur tufts at the fetlock and knee joints, planning rings of small fur-card elements angled around those joints with a puffy cloud sphere cluster, then setting the radius values for the leg segments themselves.

I'm thickening the forearm radius profile for front and hind legs so they taper naturally from muscle to ankle, and deciding on a coat gradient—jade scales fading toward cream socks with a gold cuff—using a position-based fur edge function to control where the fur teeth get shorter below the knee.

For the overall coat paint, I'm layering a cel-shaded scale texture with ink outlining in a dark teal tone for an anime-style edge, choosing scale size and paint resolution (2048) to keep texture density reasonable across the body and legs.

Weighing texture resolution tradeoffs, I decide to keep the paint sheet at 1024, giving fine enough texel density for scales while limiting total painted area to larger body parts—small pieces stay flat-colored to respect the 64-color palette limit, so I'm trimming flat colors down to around 25. Now I'm sketching the tail as a flowing cloud/flame-like tuft chained from the hips, starting a catmull-rom path from the rump root point.

Defining tail spline points...

Since flow is flattened onto the surface, tangent should align with the surface naturally, which works well for the tail sweep skin. For card count, I'm budgeting around 600-800 cards at roughly 16 triangles each with bending, landing near 10k triangles, comfortably within a 60k triangle budget.

Now I'm working out the neck-to-head attachment, tapering the neck radii from about 0.16 down to 0.09 as it rises from the chest, with the neck path starting where the spine chain ends near the chest joint.

The neck curve runs from the chest base upward through several points toward the head origin, giving a length around 0.6 units that scales proportionally with the body. I'm adjusting the head's attachment point to sit at the neck's end, recalculating the head center coordinates accordingly.

Working out total body length from rump to nose tip, roughly 2.65m plus tail, fitting the horse-like scale fine. I'm defining the head joint at the neck's terminus with a downward pitch direction, attaching it to the head group with the proper role label.

Now adding a jaw joint attached to the head, positioned slightly below and forward with its own aim vector, making sure the coordinate helper function returns properly typed tuples. I'm also setting up normalized direction vectors for the head's forward and up axes to use as reference frames for subsequent joints.

For the eyes and skull, I'm positioning a sphere geometry at the skull center using the forward direction vector as orientation, scaled to an elongated oval shape, and reusing the same head paint material with teal scales for the top of the skull.

For the muzzle, I want the top half to be jade with a cream underside, achieved by layering a countershade effect inside the cel shader to create a gradient based on surface normal direction. Then I'm placing eye decals by finding a surface point on the skull and mirroring their position for left/right symmetry.

I should check the hit result could be null and handle that with a conditional instead of forcing it, and make sure eyes aren't visually obscured by other features like brows or ears. I'm also thinking about adding a forehead ornament—a glowing jade gem shape mounted on the head bone with a gold diadem frame surrounding it.

I'm working out the orientation for a gold teardrop plate on the forehead, computing the surface normal so it faces forward correctly given the forehead's up-tilted slope, and considering a simpler tilted orientation to keep the geometry straightforward.

I'm computing the skull surface height at that forehead position, getting about 0.123 in head-local coordinates, and placing the plate there with a small embed thickness. I need to double check how the normal direction (0,0.7,0.7) in world space translates relative to the head's own coordinate frame before finalizing orientation.

Now I'm planning additional ornament details beyond the antlers and gem: a gold neck collar with pendant, a jade-studded girth band at the spine, and cloud-scroll shoulder decorations using card clusters and a swirling Chinese-style decal pattern across the flanks.

Working out decal placement...

Still writing the cloud spiral paths...

Now shifting to gold cuffs with tassels on the legs, planning to use torus geometry positioned along the leg's tangent direction at a point near the joint.

Sizing the torus to match the hexagonal tube radius, then adding a small spike underneath as a simple dangling tassel rather than modeling cloth. I'm moving on to plan the cloud mane elements—neck cards and ribbons, shoulder puffs, and a chest cloud ruff below the front of the neck.

For the mane and tail, I'm planning gradient-colored card textures running from teal roots to white/pink tips, blending two wisp palettes (teal-cream and lilac-pink) for pastel anime variety, with darker inked outlines layered beneath the main wisp shape for definition, while also considering spiral cloud scrolls at the mane ends and dorsal cloud spikes running along the spine.

Writing SVG path data...

Still defining the puff texture...

I'm deciding to skip any floating mist beneath the hooves to keep solid floor contact, and confirming the four-leg rest pose with the tail extended behind stays as planned, then adding a chest bulge for the belly.

Defining leg radius tapers...

Checking that all ground contacts, tail, whiskers, and fetlock cards stay above the floor plane, then confirming the limb helper's return type gives joint positions from root to end.

For the hind and front legs, I plan to pass hip/shoulder points and foot targets as coordinate tuples, which should match the expected point type, and set direction bends per inner joint as simple axis-aligned arrays. I'll attach each leg chain to the nearest spine joint, with front legs parenting to an upper spine joint.

For leg joint names, I'm giving each side unique labels: front legs get shoulder/elbow/knee/hoof with an L or R suffix, and hind legs get hip/stifle/hock/hoof with matching suffixes, making sure names don't collide between front and hind limbs.

For the hoof bone reference I'll grab the last joint in the chain's joints array rather than relying on a nullable tip property. Then I'm setting up color constants like gold and ink tones, planning to use cel-shaded paints for larger body parts and flat colors for smaller details to keep visual consistency.

Setting up imports and helpers...

I need to be careful to only import what's actually used, since unused imports will error. I'm also starting to draft the metadata object with name, description, and style fields for this Qilin creature.

Setting up helper functions to compute head position vectors and defining the color palette with jade and aqua tones for the design...

Still defining color constants...

I'll skip the lilac stripe idea and focus on separating head and muzzle coats, applying fur-edge shading with cream tones and a slightly different normal-based level for the muzzle underside to create natural contrast.

Now I'm setting up the qilin's skeletal builder, starting with the hips joint as the root and building a spine chain via a catmull curve through several points, checking whether group and role options are valid for the chain call.

I'm sweeping the spine to form the body, defining radius functions for rump, mid, and chest sections that taper and deepen, and working through TypeScript typing concerns for the tuple return type of the radius function.

I'm also figuring out the rump's rounded end cap placement — adjusting the extend offset so the dome doesn't push the rump too far back, settling on a smaller extension to land the rump end around z=-0.87, and noting where the tail root attaches near z=-0.85.

Now I'm moving to the chest and neck. The chest's round cap should sit at the spine's forward end before the neck begins, with the front leg root slightly forward of the shoulders. For the neck, I'm defining a curved path rising from the upper spine to the head, building it as a chain of segments and sweeping a tapering tube shape along it, with the coat color applied and a cap buried into the skull at the far end. I'm also considering increasing the number of sides on the body's cross-section for smoother shading.

Now I'm laying out the head parts: the skull as a sphere, an upper muzzle swept with a tapering radius colored for the muzzle, a lower jaw swept similarly with a cream-ish tone and rounded caps, a wispy beard card near the jaw, and small dark nostril spheres positioned near the muzzle tip.

Working out the fang placements along the muzzle underside, calculating the centerline position and radius at f=0.4 so the spikes sit flush against the lip curve.

I'm checking whether the lower jaw overlaps the muzzle bottom when closed, and adjusting the jaw's center points and radii so there's a visible mouth line instead of the jaw hiding inside the muzzle.

Adding mouth interior shapes...

Shaping the brow taper with a gold-teal gradient sweep, then planning cheek frill wisps and ear geometry -- extruding the ear outward and back with a defined outline thickness and axis orientation.

For the inner ear, I'm working through the normal vector math to figure out which face to offset the pink inner-ear extrude onto, but the mirrored side flips the direction awkwardly. I'll sidestep that by just making the inner ear its own separate, slightly smaller extrude instead of trying to pick a face.

Still refining ear shading logic...

I'm defining the ear outline as a sequence of points tracing a counter-clockwise shape from the base up to a sharp tip and back down, with smoothing applied to round out the curve while keeping the tip pointed.

Now I'm planning the rest of the character's gold accents and features: possible antlers with glowing tips, wavy gold whiskers, a forehead gem and plate, and anime-style eyes with a gold amber iris to contrast against the jade skin. I'm considering whether to keep the default pink blush, since it might look odd on a scaled face but could still work for a cute anime aesthetic.

Writing eye texture function...

Next I'm moving on to building the neck mane, generating frames positioned along the neck tube.

That's roughly 1100 triangles for the mane alone. Now I'm working out the dorsal crest along the spine chain with smaller frames tapering from withers to rump, then adding a shoulder/chest ruff with frames wrapping around the lower front of the body.

I want the chest ruff wisps to flow downward and back for a natural hanging look, then add small fringe wisps along the belly line and puffy cloud texture clusters at the shoulder and hip for extra volume.

Still clustering shoulder puff spheres...

Placing fine fluff near the fetlock around y≈0.2, with a gold cuff slightly higher near y≈0.33, plus a small tuft ring at the knee joint for added detail, then moving on to plan a hock tuft for the hind leg.

Computing the hock position along the leg segments, I'm placing a ring of five wisps there with varying sizes, defaulting their flow direction backward-down. Then I'm setting up the tail plume, arranging tube frames at three angles around the tail with growing sizes as it curves downward.

Now I'm defining two tail wisp calls -- a base segment and an end segment with larger sizes -- using the tangent direction as the flow input, plus lean and bend values. For the tail tip, I'm figuring out where the curled spiral should begin, computing the tail's end point and setting an axis and center so the spiral radiates outward from that tip while staying clear of the floor.

Working out tail curl placement...

The spiral should begin at the attachment point on the neck and curl outward with shrinking radius, so it reads as a swirl anchored to the surface. For the mirrored pair I need to flip the turn sign when the axis is mirrored, but since I'm using the same axis orientation for both sides, I can keep the same turns value and they'll match symmetrically when viewed from the side.

I'm also inventory-checking other ornamental pieces: gold swirl brooches (skip for now), hooves and dewclaws (described, dewclaw skipped), eyes and eyelashes (already in the texture), plus additional accents like a chest medallion with jade gem, anklets with tassels, horn-caps, hoof rims, and a tail ring with a gold band and jade gem. I'm setting up a girth band using a loop around the second spine joint with a slight lift.

For the girth loop itself, I'm positioning it at the spine2 joint so the cross-section plane cuts cleanly through just the torso (avoiding the legs), sweeping a thin gold tube around that loop, then placing small studs along it -- alternating gold and jade spheres using a closure counter to track every third stud for the jade gem color.

Now I'm figuring out flank decals: I want them placed where they won't collide with the girth band or the hind thigh bulk, so I'm nudging the decal's z-position forward slightly from the girth's z≈-0.15 to around z=0.2, keeping its size modest so it sits cleanly between the girth and shoulder puff regions.

I'm skipping the second decal near the haunch since the hind thigh geometry already covers that area, but I'm considering adding a swirl decal onto the thigh surface itself, computing its position and size relative to the thigh sweep so it stays per-side and attaches properly to that leg's own sweep target.

Now I'm working out the cream sock marking using a fur-edge/cel approach keyed by position along the leg, tuning the tooth and period for a jagged sock edge, then setting up the hoof color paint, the antler burr ring geometry at the base, before moving on to writing out the full paths.

I'm considering mane ribbons as beziers swept along the neck crest for solid silhouette, but deciding they're too thin to be worth it and skipping them in favor of curls and cards instead. I'm also noting that the texture SVGs will be generated via a helper function with unique gradient IDs per document, which should be safe to construct independently.

Now I'm writing the wisp generator function, building a layered SVG gradient and path outline for the wisp shapes...

I'm sketching a second curlier S-shaped flame variant for the wisp, planning to reuse the same shape function with a different color palette.

I'll set up a cloud puff SVG using overlapping circles with a vertical gradient fill.

Drawing silhouette outlines...

Building the skeleton structure...

Setting up the tail gradient paint between jade and cream tones, then moving to defining limb geometry for front legs using a side-loop helper.

That confirms the plane is YZ, which checks out. Now I'm sweeping the leg with a tapered radius profile across six keyframes, shrinking from the upper arm down through the elbow and knee region, checking that the radius values align reasonably with the joint positions along the limb.

Adjusting the radius keys to better match a fatter forearm, then placing cloven hoof tips as two small cylinders at the final leg joint, scaled along the z-axis to spread them into toe shapes with a gap between the pair.

I'm checking that the foot sits flush on the floor and considering whether to add a dark cleft detail or a gold rim ring around the hoof, working out how a torus would need to be oriented since its default plane doesn't match the vertical axis I want.

Now I'm placing a gold coronet band, then adding a cuff torus at the leg's 0.8 position using the chain point's frame and tangent for orientation, with fluff placed further along at 0.93.

I'm sizing the torus so its inner edge sits slightly embedded in the leg, then adding a tassel spike hanging from the front of the cuff, computing its base position offset from the chain point toward the leg's front face.

Actually, I'll skip the tassel and instead add a small gem — an octahedron at the front of the cuff, attached rigidly to the knee-span joint since the cuff sits past the knee.

Now I'm building the hind leg: generating limb points for hip/stifle/hock/hoof with a radius sweep for the thigh and gaskin, plus fluff near the fetlock and a haunch muscle bulge starting at the hip.

Moving to head detail, I'm defining a head bone and painting the skull with jade on top and sides, cream underneath, skipping a nose ridge bump. For the chin beard, I'm placing five jaw-anchored cards using a frame function with lilac wisp texture, downward flow, and a lean angle.

Adding cheek frills...

Now I'm defining the antNow building the antler geometry: sweeping curved beams out from the head base with tapering radius and a gold gradient coloring from base to tip.

Adding the side tines branching off the main beam at a few points along its length, each forking outward and upward toward a tip using a bezier curve with its own tapered sweep radius.

I'm also placing small glowing octahedron gems at each tine tip and the main beam tip, giving around eight glow pieces per side.

Adding ring and taper geometry...

Still shaping whisker curves...

Moving to eyes, I need them positioned so brow geometry and decals don't block visibility. For the neck, I'm building a collar loop on the neck surface and sweeping it into a gold band, anchoring it to the neck's first bone joint for rigidity rather than letting it blend across multiple bones.

Checking the blending window at that joint, I decide the default mixed-weight behavior keeps the ring consistent rather than diverging during flex tests, so I'll stick with the path's own default weighting instead of forcing a single bone. For the pendant, I'm placing it at the midpoint of the collar loop using an octahedron shape to form a gold teardrop.

Girth loop should work similarly. I'll add a gold band at the tail as well, placed near its base, and make sure the mane card frames and sweep points are typed correctly for the cards function. Eyes are already handled via the skull decal, so I'm moving on to double-check surface references.

I'm confirming the skull surface reference is correct, then adding a jaw pose rotation around the x-axis to open the mouth slightly and reveal teeth and tongue, keeping the rest of the pose neutral. I'll skip a nose ring detail and start thinking about the chest ruff before moving to the spiral curls code.

Writing curl generation function...

For the neck curls, I'm placing the curl origin at a point on the neck tube and offsetting the spiral center perpendicular to the sweep axis, making sure the center and origin share the same x-coordinate so the perpendicularity constraint holds.

I'm skipping the shoulder curls and moving to a helper for clustering cloud puffs, trNow I'm designing a cloud puff cluster helper that scatters several icosahedron bumps aroundNow I'm designing a cloud puff helper that clusters several icosahedron bumps around a bone, offsetting each bump in x, y, z with a scale factor so they form an irregular cloud shape, mirroring the x offsets based on a side parameter.

I'm placing cloud clusters at the shoulders and haunches, calculating their positions relative to the thigh and hip bones, and deciding to drop a conflicting thigh decal in favor of a flank decal instead. I'm also settling on the texture palette — teal/aqua, lilac/pink, and gold/cream wisp gradients plus a cloud texture — and starting to lay out the neck card rows using random seeds for variation.

Now I'm tallying up the total card count across neck, body, chest, belly, head, tail, whiskers, and fetlocks, landing around 300 cards at roughly 5k polygons, and adjusting mane row density to boost coverage. I'm also sizing out the texture atlas for wisps, cloud, decals, eyes, and the paint sheet, then planning to add qilin-specific touches like a jade-glowing antler, scales, and cloud-flame fetlocks before writing the final code.

Checking color strings for gems, fangs, mouth, tongue, and nose paints, then verifying type correctness across the sweep function's color paint, pair tuple returns, lambda radius typing, and scale number arrays. Confirming the cards flow function parameter types match CardOptions and that unused frame parameters are fine with underscore naming, plus validating the sweep point's tangent getter returns a proper vector.

Working through the decal placement for swirl patterns on the body surface, reasoning about mirroring: viewing from the left flank along the negative-x axis with y as up, I work out that the viewer's right points toward negative-z (toward the tail), but since my swirl design is already symmetric, no mirroring adjustment is actually needed.

Gold decals on teal body give good contrast, and the belly color and lower jaw bone setup both look fine. For the eyes, I'm using the skull's pitch and azimuth to compute ray directions at roughly ±50° that should intersect the ellipsoid head shape with the correct half-widths.

Checking the eye decal sizing against the skull radius shows the ±0.075 width spans roughly 25° to 75° in azimuth, which works for projecting along the surface normal. I'm adding eyelid ridge detail and confirming decal options like size and mirror render correctly on the jade skin tone, then positioning ears and antler base relative to the eyes using the skull's H-coordinate system.

Writing ear geometry...

Checking the cross product for the mirrored ear orientation to confirm the normal still points forward-up correctly on the opposite side.

Now I'm writing the paint condition for the ear's inner surface, checking the normal direction and position bounds to carve out the ear canal shape.

Writing SVG swirl paths...

Adding gold highlights and gem circle...

Setting up the build function with a seeded random generator and defining the teal color palette for the body paints.

Still defining paint colors...

Now I'm building the tail using a catmull spline chain with tapered sweep radii, then setting up the plume positions with a gradient fill.

Writing plume card logic...

I'm making sure the tail tip hangs down with the plume cards leaning along the tangent, keeping the bottom above floor level, and adding curls near the tail end.

For leg fluff, I'm setting up sweep frames along the legs with small flattened cards leaning outward, using wispy pastel textures for the fetlock tufts and a cloud puff texture for the knee fluff.

I should give each card-rendering call its own fresh seeded RNG so hooks don't collide, and double-check that every declared constant actually gets used—things like hips, glow, bezier curves, spiral/catmull paths, frame and limb helpers, and the ink color should all be wired in, while unused ones like countershade or gradient get dropped if not needed.

Writing brow and forehead plate geometry...

Adding the forehead gem placement as an octahedron glow near the plate, then planning cheek and eyebrow details, hair wisps across frames, and double-checking that card mesh helper usage is correct before finalizing the geometry code.

Still writing types...
